content: {"rule":"K-G4","applies":"no","applies_why":"The judge text does not quote or count any cited-in verse as an unanswered witness; it instead labels Matthew 1:16 underdetermined and notes that the relevant points were answered.","verdict":"CLEAN","quote":"D1 vs C2 (Matthew 1:16): UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings; the defender answered the beget-pattern and naming witnesses in [CR3] LINK 4 and [CR2] §5, and the challenger answered hēs in [DR3] C2.","rule_words":"A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. A verse the judge says was answered is not counted.","room":"none","why":"Because the text treats the relevant witnesses as answered and does not count any verse as an unanswered witness toward a broken link, it does not perform the act K-G4 governs."}
